attrs.label: What is local SEO?
attrs.html:
What is local SEO?

Local SEO is the work that gets a business found when people nearby search for what it sells. It covers your Google Business Profile, the map pack (the three places shown on the map), reviews, listings on other sites and the pages on your website. Unlike national SEO, it focuses on the searches people make in the areas you serve, the ones most likely to turn into a call or a visit. Google ranks local results on three things:

  1. 01

    Relevance

    How well your profile and pages match the search: the right categories, services and words your customers use.

  2. 02

    Distance

    How close you are to the person searching, or to the area they name. Location pages help you show up beyond your street.

  3. 03

    Prominence

    How well known and trusted you are: reviews, ratings, citations, local links and mentions across the web.

attrs.label: Local SEO services that win local search
attrs.html:
Local SEO services that win local search

Everything we handle, and what you’ll see in your reports.

A profile that wins clicks and calls

We complete and optimise every part of your Google Business Profile: categories, services, photos, products, posts and booking links. Then we keep it fresh every week.

  • Categories and services set correctly
  • Weekly posts and photo updates
  • Calls, bookings and clicks tracked

Common question

How do you optimise a Google Business Profile for local SEO?

Choose the most accurate primary category, add every service and service area, and complete your hours, attributes, photos and booking link. Then keep the profile active with weekly posts, new photos and quick replies to reviews. A complete, active profile is more likely to appear in the map pack, and to get the call.

Into the top three on Google Maps

The map pack gets most of the clicks for local searches. We work on the signals that move you up in Google Maps: relevance, distance and prominence.

  • Map rankings checked across your whole area
  • Profile and website signals aligned
  • Competitor gap analysis

Common question

How do you get into Google’s local 3-pack?

Google chooses the three places on the map by relevance, distance and prominence. Improve relevance with the right categories and service pages, reach further than your street with location pages, and build prominence with reviews, consistent listings and local links. Track progress with a rank grid, because rankings change from street to street.

The same name, address and phone everywhere

Search engines trust businesses whose details match across the web. We audit every local citation, fix wrong listings and add you to the directories that matter in your industry.

  • Full citation audit
  • Fixes for old or wrong details
  • New listings on trusted directories

Common question

Do citations still matter for local SEO?

Yes, but accuracy matters more than numbers. Google checks your name, address and phone number across the web, so wrong or duplicate listings can hold you back. Apple, Bing, the main data providers and the directories your customers use count most. Hundreds of low-quality directories add very little.

Reviews that build trust and rankings

Good reviews help you rank and convince people to choose you. We set up simple ways to ask for reviews and help you reply to every one.

  • Review request emails and QR codes
  • Reply templates in your voice
  • Alerts for negative reviews

Common question

How many Google reviews do you need to rank locally?

There’s no fixed number. What helps is a steady flow of new reviews, a strong average rating and a reply to every review, compared with the competitors near you. Reviews that mention your service and area also help Google, and AI assistants, understand what you do. Never buy reviews or reward customers for them.

Local landing pages for every area you serve

Each location or service area gets its own useful page, with local details, reviews, FAQs and a map, instead of thin copies of the same text.

  • Unique content for each area
  • Clear calls to book or visit
  • Linked from your profile

Common question

Do you need a separate page for each location or service area?

Yes, if you want to rank in each one. Every branch, and each main area you serve, needs its own page with real local details: the address or coverage, opening hours, reviews, directions and answers to local questions. Copying one page and swapping the town name rarely ranks, and can hold the whole site back.

Links that prove you’re part of the area

Links from local news, associations, partners and events tell Google you’re a real, trusted local business. We find and earn them for you.

  • Local press and community links
  • Partner and supplier pages
  • No paid or spammy links

Common question

What makes a good local backlink?

A link from a real, relevant website in your area: local news, a chamber of commerce or trade association, an event you sponsor, or a supplier or partner. A few links like these count for more than many links from unrelated sites, and they send visitors who are nearby and ready to buy.

The searches people make in each area

We find what people search for in each neighbourhood and service, how often, and where you rank today, so every page and post has a clear target.

  • Keywords for every service and area
  • “Near me” and area-name searches
  • Current rank for each one

Common question

How do you find local keywords for your business?

Start with each service you offer, then add the ways people search for it locally: “near me”, the area or neighbourhood name, and urgent versions such as “emergency” or “open now”. Search data shows how often each phrase is used, while Google’s suggestions and your own call notes show the exact words customers use.

Structured data for local businesses

Schema markup tells search engines your business type, address, hours, service areas and ratings in a format they read directly.

  • LocalBusiness schema on every location page
  • Opening hours and service areas
  • Checked in Google’s testing tools

Common question

Which schema markup does a local business need?

LocalBusiness schema, or a more specific type such as Dentist, Plumber or Restaurant, on your homepage and on every location page. Include your name, address, phone number, opening hours and the areas you serve. It helps Google and AI assistants read your details correctly, and you can check it with Google’s Rich Results Test.

items.question: How much does local SEO cost?
items.answer: It depends on how many locations you have, how many areas you want to rank in and how competitive your industry is. We quote every local SEO package after a free call, so you only pay for what you need.

items.question: How long does local SEO take?
items.answer: Profile and citation fixes can show movement within weeks. Ranking in the top three across a wider area usually takes a few months, depending on competition.

items.question: What is the difference between local SEO and regular SEO?
items.answer: Regular SEO helps you rank nationally or worldwide for broad searches. Local SEO focuses on searches in the areas you serve, including the map pack, and on actions like calls, visits and bookings.

items.question: What are citations in local SEO?
items.answer: Citations are mentions of your business name, address and phone number on other websites, such as directories and maps. When they match everywhere, Google trusts your details more.

items.question: Do reviews help local rankings?
items.answer: Yes. The number, quality and freshness of reviews, and how you reply to them, all help you rank and win the click. We never buy or fake reviews, as that breaks Google’s rules.

items.question: Do I need a physical address to rank locally?
items.answer: Service-area businesses can rank without showing an address, as long as the profile is set up correctly. We’ll check what’s right for your business.

items.question: Can you help with more than one location?
items.answer: Yes. We manage profiles, pages and reporting for multi-location businesses and franchises, with a clear view of each branch.

items.question: How do you report on local SEO?
items.answer: Each month you get rank grids, profile performance (calls, directions, clicks) and the enquiries tracked on your website, with clear next steps.

items.question: Do you offer white-label local SEO for agencies?
items.answer: Yes. We deliver local SEO under your brand for agencies. See our white-label SEO service.
